story_text.value:
I built a Podcasting 2.0 player that's been in the App Store for a few years. It's called Digilore™. I recently did a full comparison with the help of AI of it to all other Podcasting 2.0 apps listed at https://podcastapps.com/ (Run by Podcasting 2.0/Podcastindex.org)

It's a totally free app with no servers and collects no personal data. It does accept gifts via in app purchases.

Made for you, with love. It's written in Flutter and Dart which was a delight to use. It's recently been vibe coded with care. Beta release active now with many new exciting features such as on-device transcription and clipping for social media. Happy podcast listening!

title.value: Show HN: Comparison of Podcasting 2.0 players with Digilore

story_text.value:
I built Sidelong because I wanted one single place to store, search, and summarize all the stuff I was reading, watching, and listening to.

Save any link, article, podcast, youtube video, local file, or a bunch of other content types. Sidelong presents and embed the content, summarizes the top insights. You can subscribe to newsletters and get them sent and ingested directly, and follow your favorite podcasts and youtube channels to have the new episodes ready for you automatically. Highlight or take notes on what was interesting in anything above right in the app.

Sidelong takes what you learn, and gives you a daily summary that connects dots across the sources you saved. It also learns about your interests and recommends what you might want to check out next.

If you ever wanted to write about the stuff you're learning, you can use the built in editor which connects what you are writing with all the things you saved and presents it to you while you right.

Alot of other features like MCP, AI chat, etc as well.

title.value: Show HN: Sidelong – read-it-later and highlighting for every type of content

story_text.value:
Codeword is a cipher crossword with no clues - just a grid with numbers 1-26 on it, each corresponding to A->Z and forming words across/down, plus a few revealed starting letters. Your goal is to figure out what all the hidden letters and words are.

Codeword puzzles are generated daily, and I personally found then rather fun to solve. The hint functionality can help if you get stuck, and both generation and hints are powered by a solver, which also ended up being neat to build; https://blog.dawnofthe.dad/posts/codeword-solver/ covers that in some detail.

story_text.value:
Hi HN, I'm Fengli, founder of Inxpanse. HeyCube is our first product: the personalized feed for your always-on AI agents.

While building my own always-on agents, I kept watching the token and search API costs add up really fast. Then I noticed the scheduled tasks in ChatGPT/Grok Bot/etc. also use up a lot of your plan's allowance, often on checks that find nothing new. That's why many people still don't leave their agents truly always on.

This reminded me of the eras we humans have been through too: first search engines, then feeds. So I thought, why not build agents a feed of their own? That's why we built HeyCube. It reads sources around the clock and sends what fits you to the right agent, so your tokens go to the work itself. It's free and live at heycube.ai now, and works with ChatGPT, Grok Bot, Muse, Claude Code, and other agents in beta.

I'm looking forward to you giving your agents a feed and seeing what they can do. Let me know if you have any questions/comments/feature requests :) Thanks!

title.value: Show HN: HeyCube – The personalized feed for your always-on AI agents
